pr_body:
In the same vein as https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/20742, we record all repo mapping entries used during the load of a .bzl file too, including any of its `load()` statements and calls to `Label()` that contain an apparent repo name.

See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/20721#issuecomment-1883849462 for a more detailed explanation for this change, and the test cases in this commit for more potential triggers.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/20721
pr_title: Let .bzl files record their usages of repo mapping

review_comment: Would this impact error reporting in other cases where this isn't expected? Would `env.getValueOrThrow` be sufficient for our use case?

I couldn't for the life of me get this thing to work with `env.getValueOrThrow` 😅 For some reason, I can't use `getOrThrow` to "swallow" the exception. It seems that Skyframe always expects me to massage the exception and throw something else, instead of allowing me to say "it's fine, I got it handled"; the exception always ends up bubbling up. Here's a failed attempt if you're curious: https://gist.github.com/Wyverald/bdca2d5b1b1657db683b7f61c1ffedd1

> Would this impact error reporting in other cases where this isn't expected?

But also, just to this point -- `RepositoryMappingValue.key()` has never been used with a nonexistent repo up until now. It was only ever used by something within an existing repo, to figure out the mappings for that repo.
Thanks for trying, it wasn't clear to me whether `env.getValueOrThrow` was just meant as a way to improve error details during bubbling or as some kind of "let me try something else" mechanism.
Confirmed with @michaeledgar; once a SkyFunction throws, its node is marked as failed. So we aren't really meant to "recover" from this.
